summary: Full-site UI/UX audit of the Ryan Realty site from captured screenshots: per-page review across 7 dimensions, cross-cutting nav/design/conversion/states review, adversarial verification of P0/P1 findings.

findings.title: Site ships two entirely different global headers depending on the page — the identity of the nav changes mid-journey on the core home to search path
findings.evidence: home-desktop-01.png, listing-detail-desktop-01.png, about-desktop-01.png, contact-desktop-01.png all render the KbNav bar (uppercase serif: HOMES · COMMUNITIES · CITIES · SELL · ACCOUNT · MENU+). search-desktop-01.png renders a completely different SiteHeader (Title Case sans: Homes · Sell · Market · Guides · About + Sign in / Get listing alerts / What's my home worth). Confirmed in app/layout.tsx lines 126-132: layout renders <SiteHeader/> globally while the homepage 'carries its own KbNav + KB footer'; 58 pages import KbNav, search imports SiteHeader.
findings.fix: Consolidate to ONE header component sitewide. Recommend keeping the SiteHeader IA + persistent conversion CTAs (clearer for conversion) and applying the brand display treatment to it, then delete KbNav — or vice versa, but exactly one header must render on every public route. A user must never see the header change between home, search, and listing.
findings._verify_note: Verified directly in the screenshots. home-desktop-01, listing-detail-desktop-01, and about-desktop-01 all render the same KbNav: transparent overlay, serif "Ryan Realty" logo, uppercase serif items HOMES · COMMUNITIES · CITIES · SELL · ACCOUNT · MENU+, no persistent CTAs. search-desktop-01 renders an entirely different SiteHeader: solid navy bar, Title Case sans nav with dropdown chevrons (Homes · Sell · Market · Guides · About) plus three conversion CTAs (Sign in / Get listing alerts / What's my home worth). The two headers diverge on styling, typography, information architecture (different top-level destinations), and CTAs. A user on the core home→search path sees the global nav's identity and its advertised destinations completely change. Not a misread; real and correctly diagnosed. Held at P0 because it is the global navigation fracturing on the primary conversion funnel, with the divergence reaching the IA level — a systemic wayfinding/brand-coherence defect, not cosmetic. (The only argument for downgrade is that both navs remain functional, but the impact on the site's most important journey justifies the top severity.)

findings.title: Top-level nav items and their depth differ between the two headers — the same destination lives at a different level depending on the page
findings.evidence: home-desktop-01.png top level is HOMES, COMMUNITIES, CITIES, SELL, ACCOUNT. search-desktop-01.png / state-nav-siteheader-desktop.png top level is Homes, Sell, Market, Guides, About — Communities and Cities are demoted inside the Homes dropdown, while Market/Guides/About are promoted to top level and absent as top-level KB items. A user who learned COMMUNITIES/CITIES as primary tabs cannot find them as tabs after landing on search.
findings.fix: Define a single top-level IA and use it in the one consolidated header. Pick the 5 primary destinations once and keep Communities/Cities at a consistent depth across every page.
findings._verify_note: Verified both screenshots directly. home-desktop-01.png top-level nav = HOMES/COMMUNITIES/CITIES/SELL/ACCOUNT/MENU+ (all caps, transparent-over-hero header) — COMMUNITIES and CITIES are primary tabs. state-nav-siteheader-desktop.png is a completely different navy header with top-level Homes/Sell/Market/Guides/About (Title Case) plus Sign in/Get listing alerts/What's my home worth; its expanded Homes mega-menu shows CITIES and COMMUNITIES demoted into dropdown columns. So Communities/Cities live at top level on home but one level down on search, while Market/Guides/About are top-level on search but not on home. Two distinct header components with divergent IA — exactly as claimed. Not P0 because destinations remain reachable (Communities/Cities are still in the dropdown, nothing is dead), but this is a genuine, global, structural navigation inconsistency, correctly severed at P1.

findings.title: Nav casing and type register clash between headers (ALL-CAPS serif vs Title Case sans)
findings.evidence: about-desktop-01.png and contact-desktop-01.png render nav labels in all-caps Amboqia serif; search-desktop-01.png renders Title Case Geist sans. Same navigational role, two different brand voices — reads as two different websites and undermines the 'one polished brand' impression.
findings.fix: Standardize nav label casing and typeface as part of the single-header consolidation. One casing rule, one font for the nav across the whole site.
findings._verify_note: Underlying issue is real but the evidence is misread. Zoomed the top-right nav on all three screenshots at full res. about-desktop-01 and contact-desktop-01 render nav labels (HOMES COMMUNITIES CITIES SELL ACCOUNT MENU +) in ALL-CAPS but SANS-SERIF (Geist) — NOT Amboqia serif as claimed (the true Amboqia serif is visible in the hero headline 'HOMES HERE DESERVE' with heavy serifs/stroke contrast; the nav letterforms have no serifs). search-desktop-01 uses a different persistent dark-navy header with Title Case sans nav (Homes/Sell/Market/Guides/About) plus CTA buttons. So there IS a genuine two-headers inconsistency (different casing, different menu items, different shell), which is why this isn't a reject. But the specific 'ALL-CAPS serif vs Title Case sans / two different brand voices' claim is wrong on typeface — both navs are sans; the only real delta is casing + which header shell. That downgrades it from a two-typeface brand clash to a nav-casing/register consistency polish item. Both navs function; purely visual. P2, not P1.

findings.title: Auth entry point is labeled three different ways — 'ACCOUNT' vs 'Sign in' — for the same function
findings.evidence: home-desktop-01.png header says ACCOUNT; search-desktop-01.png header says Sign in; state-nav-megamenu-desktop.png groups it under 'YOUR ACCOUNT / Sign in'. A logged-out user cannot tell whether ACCOUNT logs them in, registers them, or opens a dashboard, and the word changes when they move pages.
findings.fix: Pick one auth label (e.g. 'Sign in' when logged out, first name/avatar when logged in) and use it in the single consolidated header everywhere.
findings._verify_note: Evidence verified across all three screenshots: home-desktop-01.png nav shows auth as "ACCOUNT" (all-caps); search-desktop-01.png shows a "Sign in" button; state-nav-megamenu-desktop.png shows "Sign in" under a "YOUR ACCOUNT" heading. So the label genuinely differs across pages — the finding is real, not a misread. Downgraded from P1 to P2 for two reasons: (1) "three different ways" is inflated — there are only two clickable auth labels ("ACCOUNT" vs "Sign in"); "YOUR ACCOUNT" is a megamenu section heading, and its actual link ("Sign in") matches the search header. (2) This is a labeling/consistency defect, not a functional break — nothing is blocked or lost, and "ACCOUNT" is a widely understood auth affordance, so the claimed "user cannot tell what ACCOUNT does" harm is overstated. That maps to a P2 consistency-polish issue, not a serious P1. Note: the screenshots also reveal a larger problem the finding under-scopes — home and search use entirely different header/nav systems — but judged on the auth-label claim as written, P2 is correct.

findings.title: Persistent conversion CTAs (Get listing alerts / What's my home worth) exist in the header on search pages but are absent from the KbNav header — including the high-intent listing-detail page
findings.evidence: search-desktop-01.png keeps three CTAs in the bar at all times (Sign in, Get listing alerts, What's my home worth). listing-detail-desktop-01.png (225 Vine Lane, highest-intent page) and home-desktop-01.png show the KbNav bar with NO persistent header CTA — valuation/alerts/contact are buried behind MENU+ or a hero button, so the core actions disappear exactly where a viewer is most ready to act.
findings.fix: Carry the same persistent header CTAs (What's my home worth, Get listing alerts, and a contact affordance) on every page in the consolidated header, especially listing-detail.
findings._verify_note: Factual core is verified and not a misread. search-desktop-01.png shows the product header with three persistent CTAs (Sign in, Get listing alerts, What's my home worth). listing-detail-desktop-01.png (225 Vine Lane) and home-desktop-01.png both show the KbNav header (HOMES/COMMUNITIES/CITIES/SELL/ACCOUNT/MENU+) with no persistent conversion CTA. Two different header systems genuinely exist, and the CTAs live only on the search surface. However, P1 overstates severity: the finding's claim that core actions "disappear exactly where a viewer is most ready to act" is only partly true. The home hero carries a search bar plus BROWSE and HOME WORTH? buttons, so valuation/search are relocated, not absent. The listing-detail screenshot only shows the above-the-fold hero, so a contact/tour CTA below the fold cannot be ruled out. The real, defensible defect is header inconsistency and the lack of a persistent header CTA on the KbNav pages — a coherence/CTA-placement issue with a moderate conversion angle, not a conversion-blocker. That is P2, not P1.

findings.title: Search page ships a different global nav than every other page — the top bar morphs mid-flow
findings.evidence: search-desktop-01.png shows a solid-navy header with title-case dropdown links (Homes / Sell / Market / Guides / About, each with a caret) plus three rounded pill CTAs (Sign in, Get listing alerts, white-filled 'What's my home worth'). Every other panel — home-desktop-01.png, listing-detail-desktop-01.png, sell-desktop-01.png, about-desktop-01.png, team-desktop-01.png, cities-desktop-01.png, city-bend-desktop-01.png, communities-desktop-01.png, housing-market-desktop-01.png, reviews-desktop-01.png, blog-desktop-01.png, contact-desktop-01.png, faq-desktop-01.png — uses a transparent header with the Amboqia wordmark and all-caps links (HOMES · COMMUNITIES · CITIES · SELL · ACCOUNT · MENU+) and no header CTAs. The link set, casing, and menu structure don't match, so a user who taps the hero SEARCH/BROWSE button lands on a top bar that looks like a different product.
findings.fix: Render the search/IDX surface inside the same global header used across the rest of the site (or port the marketing header's link set, casing, and Amboqia wordmark onto search). Reconcile the two IAs to one link set + one button set so the chrome does not change between the homepage and the core find-a-home surface.
findings._verify_note: Verified across four screenshots. search-desktop-01.png ships a solid-navy header with title-case dropdown links (Homes/Sell/Market/Guides/About + carets) and three pill CTAs (Sign in, Get listing alerts, white 'What's my home worth'). home-desktop-01.png, about-desktop-01.png, and cities-desktop-01.png all use the marketing header with all-caps links (HOMES·COMMUNITIES·CITIES·SELL·ACCOUNT·MENU+) and no CTAs. cities-desktop-01 sits on a solid-navy section, proving the divergence is the link set/casing/menu structure, not just hero-transparency vs scroll state. Two entirely different top-level IAs on the core find-a-home surface reached from the hero SEARCH button — a real component/IA-consistency defect, correctly severed at P1. Minor evidence overstatement: the search header actually retains the same Ryan Realty/BEND·OREGON wordmark and navy color, so 'different product' is a bit strong and the divergence is likely an embedded-IDX vendor header — but neither point refutes the confirmed nav mismatch or the fix.

findings.title: The search page wears a completely different global header/footer than the rest of the site, so mid-funnel it reads as a different website
findings.evidence: home-desktop-01, listing-detail-desktop-02, sell-desktop-01 and contact-desktop-01 all share one header: all-caps 'HOMES COMMUNITIES CITIES SELL ACCOUNT MENU+'. But search-desktop-01 shows a totally different header: sentence-case 'Homes / Sell / Market / Guides / About' dropdowns plus 'Sign in', 'Get listing alerts', 'What's my home worth' buttons, and search-desktop-02's footer uses a different taxonomy (SEARCH/COMMUNITIES/CITIES/MARKET/SELL/COMPANY/LEARN). The buyer's single most-used page looks like it belongs to another brand.
findings.fix: Render the same header/footer component on the search route as on home/listing/sell. Pick one account label ('Account' vs 'Sign in') and one nav set sitewide.
findings._verify_note: Every specific claim checks out against the screenshots. home-desktop-01, sell-desktop-01, listing-detail-desktop-02, and contact-desktop-01 all carry the identical global header: "Ryan Realty" logo + all-caps HOMES COMMUNITIES CITIES SELL ACCOUNT MENU+. search-desktop-01 carries a completely different header: solid navy bar, sentence-case dropdown nav (Homes/Sell/Market/Guides/About) plus Sign in, Get listing alerts, and a white "What's my home worth" pill. search-desktop-02's footer uses yet a third taxonomy (SEARCH/COMMUNITIES/CITIES/MARKET/SELL/COMPANY/LEARN). The nav taxonomies are mutually exclusive — Communities/Cities are unreachable from the search header, and Market/Guides/About are unreachable from the marketing header — so this is a real IA/consistency break on the primary buyer funnel page, not a cosmetic nit. Minor overstatement: the search page is NOT literally "another brand" (same serif Ryan Realty logo, same navy, same typefaces), so the visual identity is consistent; it's two divergent global nav systems. That rhetorical stretch doesn't change the underlying defect. Correctly severed at P1: high-impact and funnel-critical, but nothing is broken and brand color/logo/type are consistent, so not P0.

findings.title: The two mobile drawers are different paradigms (full-screen navy serif list vs right-side white sans accordion)
findings.evidence: state-nav-drawer-home-mobile.png is a full-screen navy takeover, serif links, flat categorized list (BUY/SELL/MARKET & AREA/THINGS TO DO), no CTA buttons. state-nav-drawer-site-mobile.png is a right-side white sheet, sans bold accordion rows with chevrons, and bottom CTA buttons (What's my home worth / Sign in). A mobile user relearns the menu depending on which page opened it.
findings.fix: Ship one mobile drawer component with one open direction, one type register, and one CTA block, matching the consolidated desktop header.

findings.title: Desktop megamenu interaction models differ — full-screen navy takeover (MENU+) vs compact white hover dropdown
findings.evidence: state-nav-megamenu-desktop.png shows MENU+ opening a full-screen navy overlay with 6 serif columns including THINGS TO DO. state-nav-siteheader-desktop.png shows the SiteHeader 'Homes' opening a compact white hover dropdown with 5 sans columns plus a 'Be first to new listings' promo card. The learned interaction (click for full takeover vs hover for panel) does not transfer between pages.
findings.fix: Adopt one megamenu pattern (recommend the scoped hover/click panel with the lead-capture card, which is more conversion-oriented) across the whole site.

findings.title: No persistent phone / click-to-call in either header; the phone appears only inside the KB menu and vanishes entirely in the SiteHeader system
findings.evidence: state-nav-megamenu-desktop.png and state-nav-drawer-home-mobile.png show 541.703.3095 at the bottom of the KB menu, but search-desktop-01.png and state-nav-drawer-site-mobile.png show no phone number anywhere. contact-desktop-01.png headline is 'CONTACT US · TALK TO A BROKER', yet there is no persistent tel: affordance in the top bar on any page. Phone contact is inconsistent and never one tap from the header.
findings.fix: Add a persistent click-to-call (tel:541.213.6706, the dotted brand voice number) or a compact 'Call' affordance in the consolidated header on every page, and keep it in the mobile drawer.

findings.title: Footer is also two systems (homepage KB footer vs global SiteFooter), mirroring the header split
findings.evidence: Code-evidenced (no footer panel in the audit set): app/layout.tsx lines 126-136 render the global <SiteFooter/> via HideChrome for all routes but explicitly note the homepage 'carries its own KbNav + KB footer'. Because the header is already two systems, the footer inconsistency compounds the 'two different sites' impression across the journey.
findings.fix: Consolidate to a single SiteFooter rendered on every public route (including the homepage) alongside the single header. Capture a footer screenshot to confirm parity before/after.

findings.title: Primary button styling and casing split between two systems (all-caps rectangular vs title-case rounded pills)
findings.evidence: home-desktop-01.png, about-desktop-01.png and sell-desktop-01.png render CTAs as all-caps, letter-spaced, near-rectangular buttons (BROWSE →, HOME WORTH?, GET MY HOME VALUE →, SEARCH). search-desktop-01.png renders header CTAs as title-case, fully-rounded pills (Sign in, Get listing alerts, white-filled 'What's my home worth', Save this search). The same action is styled two different ways — 'HOME WORTH?' as an outlined all-caps rectangle on the marketing pages vs 'What's my home worth' as a title-case white pill on search.
findings.fix: Standardize on one Button component and one casing convention for primary/secondary CTAs, then apply it to both the marketing headers and the search header. Pick either all-caps-rectangular or title-case-pill and drop the other so the same action reads the same way everywhere.

findings.title: Headline median-price stat rendered in mixed formats across surfaces ($742,000 vs $742K vs $550K)
findings.evidence: home-desktop-01.png and housing-market-desktop-01.png print the regional median as '$742,000', but cities-desktop-01.png prints the identical figure as '$742K' in its big display tile, and listing-detail-desktop-01.png shows '$550K'. The same class of headline currency stat appears in three formats within the same user flow.
findings.fix: Pick one currency format for headline stats. Brand voice calls for rounding to the nearest thousand ('$742,000'); apply it consistently, or consistently use the 'K' abbreviation on all big display tiles — but do not mix full and abbreviated formats for the same stat across pages.

findings.title: Two near-identical valuation heroes plus a form that re-asks for the address the user already typed
findings.evidence: sell-desktop-01 puts an 'Enter your home address' field + 'GET MY HOME VALUE' directly in the hero. sell-valuation-desktop-01 is a separate 'WHAT'S YOUR HOME WORTH?' hero that also just says 'GET MY HOME VALUE'. sell-valuation-desktop-02 then presents a form whose Property-address field shows the empty placeholder '123 Main St, Bend, OR 97701' — implying the address entered on /sell is not carried through. A seller hits address entry twice and two competing 'start here' pages.
findings.fix: Collapse the two valuation heroes into one canonical entry, and prefill the valuation form's address from whatever the user typed on the /sell hero so they never type it twice.

findings.title: Hero eyebrow is nearly invisible and the proof-stat line is clipped, weakening the first 3 seconds
findings.evidence: In home-desktop-01 the eyebrow 'CENTRAL OREGON REAL ESTATE' is white type sitting over bright green foliage with almost no contrast — it reads as a faint smudge. The credibility stat block ('1,871 homes... Median list $742,000... Pending in 20 days') has its last line obscured at bottom-left, so the strongest trust number ('20 days') is half-hidden.
findings.fix: Add a darkening scrim/gradient behind the eyebrow and the lower-left stat block, and add bottom padding so the '20 days' line is never clipped.

findings.title: A floating circular badge pinned to the bottom-left corner overlaps hero body copy on multiple pages
findings.evidence: A dark round 'N' element sits at the exact bottom-left corner of every panel. On content-bearing heroes it covers copy: home-desktop-01 (over 'Pending in 20 days'), contact-desktop-01 (over 'to you quickly'), sell-desktop-01 (over 'free valuation'), and sell-valuation-desktop-01 (over 'comps behind the number'). It repeatedly eats the last line of the value proposition.
findings.fix: If this is a chat/assistant launcher, move it to the bottom-right (the conventional spot) and/or reserve bottom padding in hero layouts so no copy renders beneath it.

findings.title: Contact page hero offers only 'Send a message' with no phone/email and the form pushed below the fold
findings.evidence: contact-desktop-01 fills the entire first viewport with a photo, the 'CONTACT US' headline, and a single 'SEND A MESSAGE' button that scrolls to a form. No phone or email is visible on the page (a number only appears in the footer, per search-desktop-02), even though the listing detail (listing-detail-desktop-02) surfaces a direct broker phone plus Call/Text. The dedicated contact surface is the one place hiding the fastest contact methods.
findings.fix: Put a tap-to-call phone and email directly in the contact hero (or lift the message form up into the first viewport) so reaching out takes zero scrolling.

findings.title: Seller landing page uses an off-brand orange CTA and orange stars that clash with the navy/cream system on the site it feeds into
findings.evidence: lp-seller-home-value-desktop-01 and -02 use a bright orange 'Get my home value' button and orange review stars. Every other conversion surface uses navy primaries: sell-desktop-01, sell-valuation-desktop-02 ('Get my home value' in navy) and listing-detail-desktop-02. A visitor arriving from the ad LP then clicking into the main site sees the accent color change, undercutting coherence.
findings.fix: If orange is a deliberate paid-LP contrast test, keep it but re-run the test against a navy variant; otherwise switch the CTA and stars to the brand navy so the LP matches the destination site.

findings.title: Primary seller page opens on a muddy pink/purple grainy photo that looks lower-quality than the crisp hero used elsewhere
findings.evidence: sell-desktop-01's hero is a heavily grained purple-tinted mountain image, noticeably softer and off-palette next to the sharp Old Mill drone hero on contact-desktop-01 and sell-valuation-desktop-01. This is the main seller entry point, so its first impression is doing less work than it should.
findings.fix: Swap the /sell hero to the canonical Old Mill hero (or a cleaner navy-toned photo) so the top seller page matches the polish of the valuation and contact pages.

findings.title: A dead/invalid listing URL renders a headerless, orphaned "Page not found" (no logo, no nav) unlike the polished global 404
findings.evidence: state-listing-notfound-desktop.png shows the centered "404 / Page not found" block on a bare white page with NO navy site header, no logo, and no navigation. Compare state-404-desktop.png (a true 404) which keeps the full SiteHeader + nav. Confirmed in code: lib/site/chrome-routes.ts shouldHideDefaultChrome() matches /^\/listing\/[^/]+$/ and hides the SiteHeader on listing routes; when the listing key is invalid the page throws notFound() so its own KB hero header never renders, leaving the not-found page (app/not-found.tsx) with zero chrome. Recovery links (search + browse/market/sell + homepage) exist in the body, so it is not a dead end, but with no header/logo it reads as broken. This is the exact state a user hits from a shared, stale, or sold canonical /listing/<key> link.
findings.fix: Ensure chrome renders on the listing not-found: add app/listing/[listingKey]/not-found.tsx (or make NotFoundClient self-contained with the Ryan Realty logo + a minimal nav), and treat a missing listing as sold/expired rather than generic 404 — e.g. "This home may no longer be on the market" plus a link to similar active homes in the area. At minimum, do not suppress the SiteHeader on the listing not-found path.

findings.title: Top navigation completely changes between the homepage/marketing pages and the search + login pages on the primary buyer path
findings.evidence: Marketing/KB pages use one persistent nav — uppercase serif "HOMES · COMMUNITIES · CITIES · SELL · ACCOUNT · MENU+" (home-desktop-01.png, listing-detail-desktop-01.png, about-desktop-01.png). The core search results page and auth pages use a different header — sentence-case "Homes · Sell · Market · Guides · About" plus "Sign in / Get listing alerts / What's my home worth" buttons (search-desktop-01.png, state-nav-siteheader-desktop.png, login-desktop-01.png). On the single most important journey (home → search) the labels, casing, grouping, and CTAs all change. Confirmed intentional-but-transitional in lib/site/chrome-routes.ts (search/auth are the "NOT-yet-KB siblings").
findings.fix: Unify the persistent top nav so labels and CTAs are stable across the whole journey — migrate /homes-for-sale search and the auth pages onto the KB nav (or standardize the KB pages onto the SiteHeader). Keep the same top-level items and the "What's my home worth" CTA visible on every surface.

findings.title: The same listing shows two different named brokers depending on viewport (desktop "Paul Stevenson" vs mobile "Your broker Matt")
findings.evidence: For 225 Vine Lane ($550K), listing-detail-desktop-02.png shows the sidebar "Talk to a broker" card with Paul Stevenson (Broker #201259123, phone, email, and a Paul Robinson review), while listing-detail-mobile-02.png shows the sticky bottom bar "YOUR BROKER — Matt". The desktop card (components/site/listing-detail/ListingBrokerCTA.client.tsx) SSRs the default principal broker then swaps to the attributed broker on hydration; the mobile bar (ListingMobileContactBar.client.tsx) shows a broker prop and does not apply the same attribution swap — so within one session the two surfaces can name different contacts for the same home. A buyer cannot tell who actually handles this property.
findings.fix: Resolve the broker once (same attribution/assignment logic) and feed both the desktop card and the mobile sticky bar from that single source so the named contact, phone, and photo are identical across viewports.

findings.title: Six utility/support pages reuse the identical Old Mill hero photo with identical treatment, reading as templated
findings.evidence: The exact same Old Mill drone photo (three smokestacks, flag, Deschutes River) with the same dark-gradient + white Amboqia headline + eyebrow + two-CTA layout appears on sell-valuation-desktop-01.png, lp-seller-home-value-desktop-01.png, reviews-desktop-01.png, tools-mortgage-desktop-01.png, and faq-desktop-01.png (contact reuses it too). Only the headline text changes. A visitor moving between these pages sees the identical image repeatedly, which cheapens the otherwise premium, hand-crafted feel the homepage and hubs establish.
findings.fix: Rotate distinct Central Oregon photography per utility page (the brand hero folder already carries multiple crops, and /about and /buy already use different photos). Give the valuation, FAQ, mortgage, reviews, and contact heroes their own image so no two adjacent pages share the same hero.

workflowProgress.label: verify:global:Site ships two entirely
